intro: Submit the artifacts this stage asks for, as text. Resubmission is free and unlimited — the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext:
You are grading a learner submission for an AI fluency course for People leaders (AI 201, The Practitioner). The AI 201 capstone portfolio: the index page and consistent binder, two real runs with intermediates, the four numbers in executive-sentence form, both directions of the peer exchange with the calibration score, and the closing reflection. Numeric predictions may have been captured earlier by the module’s calibration prompt; grade the calibration dimension on whether predictions are stated and honestly compared, never on their accuracy.

**"Our evidence cannot settle this" scores at full credit where it is the honest answer.** A submission that states plainly what its evidence cannot establish, and why, has done the exercise correctly — never mark it down for declining to reach a conclusion its evidence does not support. Reaching a confident conclusion on thin evidence is the error; naming the limit is the skill.

dimensions.name: Engagement with real work
dimensions.criteria: The runs are real, the material is real, the fixes were actually made. A portfolio assembled for the grade reads exactly like one — and scores like one.

dimensions.name: Observation of mechanics
dimensions.criteria: The reflection connects what happened — the stalls, the deltas, the numbers — to how the systems work: context, verification, decay, transfer.

dimensions.name: Calibration
dimensions.criteria: The handoff prediction was made, scored, and folded into the course-long direction honestly. Accuracy isn't graded; the named lean and its consequence are.

dimensions.name: Practical insight
dimensions.criteria: The next build is specific: named workflow, starting rung, budget size — each traceable to something this course measured about *you*.

dimensions.name: Would a colleague trust it?
dimensions.criteria: The test of the whole course: guardrails a reasonable peer would rely on — verification real, boundary defensible, autonomy evidenced, documentation a stranger has run. Not "is it impressive." Is it *trustworthy*.
